        The 2026 PGA Tour season has just one tournament left: the Tour Championship at East Lake Golf Club in Atlanta, which carries a $40 million purse distributed among the top 30 golfers in the FedEx Cup standings. However, big money is already being sent out at the onset of this week for FedEx Cup bonuses, which are being awarded after the BMW Championship for the first time.The winner of this week's Tour Championship will also be crowned the FedEx Cup champion, a title Tommy Fleetwood is seeking to defend. As he proved last year, winning at the right time can turn a disappointing season into a FedEx Cup championship year, but as the PGA Tour also wanted to reward season-long excellence, it has created a $100 million bonus pool from which massive checks will be sent to those atop the FedEx Cup standings coming out of the year's penultimate event.This is in addition to the $20 million purses that were on the line for the St. Jude Championship and BMW Championship, the first two legs of the FedEx Cup Playoffs. In total, $180 million will be awarded to the best golfers in the world over a three-week span. Scottie Scheffler once again enters the Tour Championship at No. 1 in the FedEx Cup standings, and for his consistency at the top all year, he earned a $23 million bonus -- $22 million in cash and a $1 million deferred payment to his pension fund. The rest of the top 10 players in the FedEx Cup standings earned over $1 million combined in cash and deferred bonuses. 
Wyndham Clark's win over the weekend at the BMW Championship jumped him from fifth to third in the FedEx Cup, which not only earned him $3.6 million for the win in Bellerive but also increased his bonus payout from $5.4 million to $8 million. Below is the complete breakdown of how the FedEx Cup bonus pool is being distributed with deferred payments going to that player's pension fund and cash payments being sent out immediately to those in the top 50. 2026 FedEx Cup bonus money, payoutsTotal pool: $100 million

title: Florida names Aaron Philo starting QB: Georgia Tech transfer tapped to lead Gators in 2026 - CBS Sports
description: What to know about the first-year starter and who he beat during fall camp
body:
What to know about the first-year starter and who he beat during fall camp
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Aug 24, 2026
                            
                    at
    12:04 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Coming out of Florida's second fall scrimmage, Gators coach Jon Sumrall named Georgia Tech transfer Aaron Philo as the team's starting quarterback ahead of next month's opener against FAU.  One of Florida's top transfers this cycle after joining former Yellow Jackets offensive coordinator Buster Faulkner in Gainesville, Philo backed up Haynes King last season and beat out Tramell Jones Jr. for the job with the Gators.Philo has received most of the first-team reps during the last week of practice and reportedly impressed during Saturday night's scrimmage, highlighted by a 15-yard touchdown run early on.Undecided on Florida's quarterback battle after spring, Sumrall said the position remained even earlier this month as both players pushed for the job. That changed after Sumrall and his offensive staff reviewed film over the weekend.He said Monday that Philo will get the "lion's share of reps" this week as game prep begins.
"We are preparing for him to be the starter for Week 1," Sumrall said.Sumrall's still a believer in Tramell JonesSumrall stressed that Philo is the starter for the first game."There will not be some crazy hoopla around it in our building, it's just how we're moving forward," Sumrall said Monday. "I met with both guys and both are awesome. I'm excited about the room. The good news is both of them have elevated their play. Love both of them and I'm fired up for both of them."It's been a real battle, it's not been some empty competition. It's been real and that's where we are."From pre-snap checks to reading defenses and being able to "kill" bad calls, Philo showed superiority.
"He has operated at the line of scrimmage at a touch higher level," Sumrall said. "There's no surprise in the spring because he'd been in the system and Tramell had not. We're able to operate the full offense at a little bit higher level with Aaron, with the whole level. Their arm talent is very similar. What's unique is both of them's play style resembles each other more than it differentiates."Sumrall also said that Philo has seen the "middle of the field" a bit more during practice."I talked to Aaron this is not an anointing," Sumrall said. "(This) is not some permanent, you're the starter forever. For Tramell, it's not like you're being relegated or demoted and forgotten. This is not fatal. I'm a believer in Tramell Jones. I just feel like right now it's where we need to go with the decision, but the guys will rally around both."
Faulkner's offensive scheme at FloridaFaulkner wants a passer who can operate quickly, distribute the football in space and punish defenses when safeties creep toward the line of scrimmage. Philo checks every box. He played with confidence at Georgia Tech, understanding leverage and has enough mobility to extend possessions without abandoning the structure of the offense. Those are two areas of strength Philo reportedly displayed during both camp scrimmages this month.Most importantly, Philo's comfortable playing aggressively. Florida needs a quarterback capable of creating explosive plays while keeping the offense on schedule, and Philo's experience in Faulkner's system should accelerate that transition. 
There will be adjustments against SEC defenses, but the scheme familiarity makes Philo a natural fit for what Florida wants offensively.

title: Dana Brown out as Astros GM; owner Jim Crane to oversee baseball operations - CBS Sports
description: The Astros currently sit tied for first place in the AL West at one game under .500
body:
The Astros currently sit tied for first place in the AL West at one game under .500
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Aug 24, 2026
                            
                    at
    9:56 am ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The Houston Astros and general manager Dana Brown have mutually agreed to part ways, the team announced Monday morning.Owner Jim Crane will oversee baseball operations "through the transition period," according to the team. Brown's responsibilities will be divided among the assistant general managers -- Charles Cook, Gavin Dickey and Connor Huff -- and senior advisor Jeff Bagwell, the Hall of Fame first baseman who spent his entire 15-year playing career with Houston."Over the past four seasons, Dana has helped our organization win two division titles and has led our baseball front office through key scouting, draft and development efforts," Crane said in a statement. "On behalf of the Astros, I want to thank him for his commitment, energy, and contributions to our organization. We wish he and his family the best."
        
            
                Seven more MLB executives who could be on the hot seat after Astros' Dana Brown
                
                    Matt Snyder                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
Brown took over the front office heading into the 2023 season, taking the helm of the defending World Series champions. The Astros won the AL West in 2023 and 2024 and advanced all the way to the ALCS in 2023. Last season, however, they missed the playoffs for the first time since 2016, and Brown entered this season as a lame duck. 
The Astros are currently tied for first place in the AL West, but sit one game under .500 at 65-66."I want to thank Jim Crane for the opportunity to serve in my first role as an MLB general manager," Brown said in a statement. "The Astros organization and the fans have welcomed me and my family, and I am grateful to have called Houston home for the past four seasons. I wish the organization well and I look forward to the future as I continue my 36-plus years in professional baseball."Brown, 59, played college ball for Seton Hall before being a 35th round draft pick and spending three years in the minors. Immediately after his playing days were concluded, he became a minor-league coach and then a scout. He worked his way up the chain for years in front offices, becoming vice president of scouting for the Braves in 2019. The Astros GM job was his first as the top decision-maker. 
Crane has been the Astros' owner since 2011. On his watch, the Astros became a powerhouse, making the playoffs eight straight seasons -- a run that includes seven division titles, four pennants and two World Series championships. Jeff Luhnow was the general manager from 2011-19, but was dismissed after the sign stealing scandal. James Click was the GM from 2020-22 and Brown took over after that.Now, with the playoffs still in sight, the Astros will be looking for a new lead executive.Inside the 2026 seasonIt's been an interesting run for the Astros this year. As noted, they are tied for first place, albeit with a sub-.500 record.
On the good side, Yordan Alvarez has put it all together -- and stayed healthy -- and is having an MVP campaign. He enters the last week of August leading the majors in on-base percentage, slugging percentage, OPS, OPS+ and total bases, while also leading the American League in average, home runs, RBI and walks. He's slashing .320/.436/.613 with 36 homers and 90 RBI. Pitching has been an issue. The Astros rank 25th in baseball with a 4.63 staff ERA. The rotation has actually been a disaster, as the Astros are 28th in the majors with a 5.15 ERA from starting pitchers. Their big free-agent signing was Tatsuya Imai, who has lost his spot in the rotation while sporting a 5.32 ERA. Curiously, the Astros added just center fielder Daulton Varsho in front of the trade deadline, when it was pretty obvious they needed rotation help.
Regardless, the Astros got hot in late July -- winning 11 of 12 at one point -- and that's enough to be relevant in the AL West.

        The 2026 U.S. Presidents Cup team is halfway filled with six players earning their way onto the squad at the conclusion of the BMW Championship. The penultimate event of the FedEx Cup Playoffs marked the end of the qualifying window for the red, white and blue in the international team event slated to take place at Medinah Country Club's Course No. 3 from Sept. 24-27.Leading the way is none other than world No. 1 Scottie Scheffler, who secured his place atop the rankings following his runaway victory at the St. Jude Championship. He is joined by Players Championship winner Cameron Young and U.S. Open winner Wyndham Clark, each of whom has put together a tremendous season.Clark not only claimed his third title of the year with his win at the BMW Championship, he managed to play his way into the top six to ensure he would be donning America's colors in Chicago next month. Clark went from No. 7 in the standings to No. 3 as Ben Griffin fell from No. 5 to No. 8 with his T44 finish at the BMW Championship.All six automatic qualifiers have experience in both the Presidents Cup and the Ryder Cup, as Clark was the only player to not tee it up at Bethpage Black in last fall's Ryder Cup.

title: Caitlin Clark hits eight 3-pointers in one of the best games of her career - CBS Sports
description: The eight 3s were a career high for Clark, who scored 37 points as the Fever beat the Sky around some courtside d
body:
The eight 3s were a career high for Clark, who scored 37 points as the Fever beat the Sky around some courtside drama
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Aug 24, 2026
                            
                    at
    9:06 am ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        CHICAGO -- Late on Sunday evening, Caitlin Clark curled toward the top of the key, took a handoff from Mercedes Russell and started to drive toward the middle of the floor. After two dribbles, she planted her right foot, went between her legs and stepped back to 25 feet. Sydney Taylor couldn't recover in time, and Clark's 3-pointer hit nothing but net. The shot was the nail in the coffin on the Indiana Fever's 113-90 win over the Chicago Sky on a chaotic night at Wintrust Arena, and gave Clark a career-high eight 3s. She finished with 37 points, three rebounds and 10 assists in the second-highest scoring outing of her career and also recorded her fifth 30-point, 10-assist game. Every single other player in WNBA history combined has four such games. "I think a mix of both," Clark said, when asked if her career night was a matter of generating good looks or just having a hot hand. As a team, the Fever shot 18 of 33 from 3-point range to set a new single-game franchise record. "I thought me and Kelsey did a really good job in the second half of playing split game and shallowing out of cuts, playing pitch and just putting them in a lot of actions where they had to pick and choose between the two of us and cause some confusion. Additionally, thought we played well in transition."30-point, 10-assist games in WNBA historyPlayer30/10 GamesCaitlin Clark5Skylar Diggins1Sabrina Ionescu1Jia Perkins1Diana Taurasi1
        
            
                Enes Kanter Freedom ejected from courtside seat at WNBA game after altercation with Sky guard Natasha Cloud
                
                    Jack Maloney                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
Sunday's game was the second of a back-to-back for the Fever and the end of a grueling road trip that saw the team travel back and forth across time zones as they played five games in eight days. They were coming off back-to-back defeats to the Dallas Wings and New York Liberty, and were without All-Star center Aliyah Boston, who was ruled out due to a leg injury. (Boston has been managing a leg issue all season, and is not expected to miss additional time.)Clark knew she had to be aggressive and look to score more than usual. 
"I think I just came in with the mentality of knowing that my team needs me to step up tonight," Clark said. "Obviously with AB going down, that hurts our team a little bit, so you gotta carry a little bit more of a load. "I think it's all about your mentality coming into a back-to-back. You can either be like, 'I'm tired, we've been on the road. This that.' Or you can buck up and go play basketball and have fun. I feel like our team had great energy coming into this game and had a great mindset about how we wanted to approach it."
It didn't take Clark long to get going. Less than a minute into the game, she already had a 3 and an assist. She finished the first quarter with eight points and four assists, but also five turnovers against a physical Sky defense. Clark settled down after that and did not have another turnover the rest of the night. The 3s, the points and the assists continued unabated. Clark had 10 points in the second, 11 in the third and eight in the fourth. She had multiple assists in every quarter and multiple 3s in three of four quarters. She made 207 feet worth of 3s, including an absurd 35-foot step-back in the third quarter. 
With the win, the Fever improved to 25-14, and set a new single-season wins record. They are percentage points behind the Atlanta Dream for the No. 4 seed and one game back of the Las Vegas Aces for third place with just one week until the league takes a multi-week break for the FIBA World Cup.

        This is an article version of the CBS Sports HQ AM Newsletter, the ultimate guide to every day in sports. You can sign up to get it in your inbox every weekday morning here. 
 🏈 Five things to know Monday NFL preseason Week 2 might have settled the Browns' quarterback battle. Although Shedeur Sanders was only decent in his first start of the preseason, he was significantly better than Deshaun Watson, and it's no overreaction to say that might be enough to win him the job. Browns fans booed Watson off the field, so it's safe to say the Cleveland community is ready for Sanders to settle in as the starter. Meanwhile, in Atlanta, Michael Penix Jr. is cleared for 11-on-11 drills and could push Tua Tagovailoa over the coming weeks. And while the Raiders have not formally named Kirk Cousins their starter, all signs point to him leading the offense in Week 1 instead of Fernando Mendoza. Speaking of all these quarterbacks, we graded all 15 of the rookies who saw the field in this week's preseason action. Elsewhere, Harrison Butker drilled a 69-yard field goal, which would be an NFL record if it happened in the regular season. Also, Ashton Jeanty sustained an injury in practice and could be in danger of missing time.Class of 2022 athletes are ineligible for college sports again -- or are they? A federal court granted the NCAA's appeal to the lawsuit that gave some athletes a fifth year of eligibility. But a large group of football and basketball players remain cleared to return to school, as the ruling does not apply to those who filed individual lawsuits. That means linebacker Trent Hendrick is allowed to transfer to UCLA after going through minicamp with the Browns, and it paves the way for former Florida State quarterback Thomas Castellanos to enter the transfer portal. In college basketball, Mark Mitchell committed to Kentucky for his extra year, which gives the Wildcats a boost in our latest Top 25 And 1.Enes Kanter Freedom was ejected from his courtside seat at the Fever-Sky game. The WNBA has become an arena for the debate surrounding transgender athletes, and Kanter Freedom is outspoken in the discourse. The former NBA player requested eligibility for the WNBA Draft and sat courtside Sunday night, and after he got into a verbal altercation with Sky guard Natasha Cloud, a game official and security personnel removed him from his seat. This incident came just three days after commissioner Cathy Engelbert denounced those who seek to use the WNBA to "sow divisiveness."The Premier League season kicked off with a few shocking results. Nobody was surprised to see Arsenal take care of business with a dominant 3-0 win over Coventry City. But Hull City's 2-0 upset of Manchester United? Yeah, that one was a stunner. Sound the alarm bells for United, and while you're at it, check Aston Villa's pulse -- the 4-0 loss to Brighton suggests they might be in for a rough start to the season. If you still haven't decided who to root for this year, check out our guide to European soccer and determine your best fit. Or maybe just support the team with the best kits.Wyndham Clark fended off Rory McIlroy to win the BMW Championship. The 30-man field for the Tour Championship is set following the second event of the FedEx Cup Playoffs. Clark entered the final round with a five-stroke lead and bounced back from a shaky start with birdies on the last three holes to hold off second-place Patrick Cantlay and third-place Rory McIlroy. In addition to the No. 3 spot in the cup standings, Clark won himself a $3.6 million payday. He stands behind only Matt Fitzpatrick and Scottie Scheffler, the latter of which battled hand, foot and mouth disease during his struggles at the BMW Championship. 🏀 Do not miss this: Coaches predict college basketball's top teams 
                                                                    Mike Meredith, CBS Sports
                                                            Every year, our Matt Norlander and Gary Parrish survey coaches across Division I men's basketball on a number of topics. One of the most highly anticipated sections of the Candid Coaches series each preseason is the one in which coaches pick the best teams for the upcoming campaign. While nine schools received votes this year, there is a consensus on the top few. Just one year removed from a national championship, Florida decidedly has the best squad in America heading into 2026-27. Of the nearly 100 coaches Norlander and Parrish surveyed, 55% voted for the Gators as the top team in the land. Anonymous coach: "Not even close, in my opinion. The combination of great returning players along with Todd Golden and Carlin Hartman at the helm is unmatched. (Denzel) Aberdeen being somewhat cleared to play a fifth year is just icing on the cake. Really tough schedule obviously, but I could see them dropping only four games before SEC tournament starts in March."A few takeaways from the poll, in which Duke, Tennessee, UConn and Illinois were also highly regarded: The Blue Devils might have the sport's deepest roster.This could be the best offense Rick Barnes has rostered since joining the Volunteers.Braylon Mullins and Silas Demary Jr. give UConn one of the nation's top backcourts.The Fighting Illini could again have a top-two offense. ⚾ Brewers stand tall atop MLB Power Rankings 
                                                                    Getty Images
                                                            Last week, the Brewers asserted themselves as the best team in baseball with a 3-1 series win over the Dodgers. That's a tough act to follow. All they did in their next time out was demolish the Mariners in a 22-0 laugher. And then they won that series and their three-game set with the Braves. This team is cooking. 
Milwaukee is not only on pace for its first 100 season, but it also has a realistic chance of winning its first World Series. It strengthened its grip on the No. 1 spot in our MLB Power Rankings, which Matt Snyder justified by listing some absurd stats: Snyder: "They have one of the best defenses in baseball (sitting sixth in defensive efficiency, for example). Despite sitting in last in home runs, they are in the top five in batting average and top 10 in OPS, checking in as one of the most prolific run-scoring teams in baseball. They sit third in stolen bases and are one of the best baserunning teams in baseball. They are second in the majors in ERA, too."As for the teams the Brewers cruised past over the past week, they are trending in all sorts of directions. 2. Dodgers (↑2) 6. Braves (↓3) 20.         The 2026-2027 Serie A season is finally back, and after the first weekend of action, it's already time to reflect on what happened and especially what we can expect ahead of the second matchday that will take place later this week. Inter won convincingly on Saturday, as the 2025–2026 Serie A champions cruised to a dominant 4–1 victory over Monza. Their title rivals responded on Sunday, with AC Milan beating Torino 2–1 and Juventus securing a narrow 1–0 win away at Frosinone, while Napoli won 2-0 at Genoa. Now, time for some hot takes:AC Milan gem takes advantage, but what about Pulisic?The biggest surprise of the first weekend of Serie A action was AC Milan wonderkid Alphadjo Cisse, who scored the opening goal of the 2-1 win against Torino on Sunday. The Italian winger, who will turn 20 in October, is highly valued by his coach Ruben Amorim, who praised him ahead of the match. "I'm in love with him," he said.The Portuguese coach, who replaced Massimiliano Allegri on the bench of the Italian giants this summer, handed Cisse his first Serie A start in his first official league match in charge. Rafael Leao is currently sidelined with an injury and is expected to leave the Rossoneri before transfer deadline day, while American Christian Pulisic is still working his way back to full fitness. It's an opportunity for Cisse to take full advantage and cement himself as the starter on the left wing. Cisse proved to be at the level asked by Amorim, and he's expected to start again on Friday when AC Milan will host Venezia. Leao and Pulisic can wait, it's now time for Cisse to shine. 
As for the American, who suffered a microfracture in his leg in the USMNT's last game at the World Cup, a 4-1 loss to Belgium, his versatility means he should see the field plenty, but a lot will depend on how Amorim evolves at the club. But Cisse's surge isn't great news for Leao, but it shouldn't impact Pulisic all that much when he's healthy.
Andy Diouf: Inter unexpected starInter started off well their debut Serie A game of the season as the 2025-2026 Scudetto winners won 4-1 against Monza at San Siro on Saturday. Hakan Calhanoglu, Francesco Pio Esposito, Yann Bisseck and Piotr Zielinski all scored in the opening game but the MVP of the match was Andy Diouf, the French winger who delivered two key assists against Monza.His performances are great news for Nerazzurri coach Cristian Chivu, who decided to deploy him as a right wing-back in Inter's 3-5-2 system last season, despite the player arriving from Lens in the summer of 2025 as a central midfielder. Last year, when Denzel Dumfries was injured, Chivu tried him in that position and improved drastically in the second part of the season, despite having said multiple times that he was not particularly keen on playing on the right wing. When the Nerazzurri sold Dumfries to Real Madrid this summer, Inter decided to sign Djed Spence from Tottenham but consider Diouf a potential starter in that position as well. In the end, Chivu was not wrong. 
The mistake of Spalletti After winning 1-0 in the opening game against Frosinone, Juventus coach Luciano Spalletti spoke about the Bianconeri striker Randal Kolo Muani, who didn't score in his Serie A debut after arriving from PSG in the summer. Spalletti, speaking to DAZN, didn't really have nice words about the French player and said, "We went and got Kolo, we've looked after him and we know what his value is. But he has to realize that he hasn't played for two years and there must be a reason for that. Sometimes you think you're at an exceptional level but you've left something behind that you need to go and get back."
It's a risky choice from Spalletti to speak about one of his best players in this way. Kolo Muani is now a key striker for Juventus after the Italian club decided to not sign a new deal with former striker Dusan Vlahovic, who ended up signing with Besiktas later in the summer transfer window. Spalletti is not new to making strong statements about his players, but comments like these could easily backfire, particularly when aimed at a player who has quickly become an important part of the team ahead of the upcoming season.

title: Dana Brown out as Astros GM: Seven more MLB executives who could be on the hot seat - CBS Sports
description: Has Mike Elias' Orioles rebuild finally run out of time? Is David Stearns actually safe? Can Buster Posey turn th
body:
Has Mike Elias' Orioles rebuild finally run out of time? Is David Stearns actually safe? Can Buster Posey turn things around for the Giants?
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Aug 24, 2026
                            
                    at
    10:52 am ET
                        
                •
            
            4 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The Astros have parted ways with general manager Dana Brown, the team announced Monday morning. He'd only been on the job since the start of the 2023 season, but he lasted longer than James Click did in that job under hands-on owner Jim Crane. The obvious next question is which front office executive(s) might be the next to go. That's just the nature of the job in this business. Now, the titles vary. Call them general manager or president of baseball operations or chief baseball officer, but we're talking about the top baseball operations decision-maker for each team. Here are seven top executives who could find themselves on the chopping block sometime soon. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Nick Krall, Reds president of baseball operationsKrall was promoted to the top baseball job in 2020, and the Reds made the playoffs last season, but that was as an 83-win team that merely served as a sacrificial lamb in the Wild Card Series to the Dodgers. They are currently seven games under .500 and not in playoff contention. The state of the roster isn't great. Player development has seen wins like Elly De La Cruz, Sal Stewart, Chase Burns and Hunter Greene. That's really about it, though. There have been so many misses otherwise. It's been more than a decade since the Reds were a strong contender.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Mike Elias, Orioles president of baseball operations and general managerElias took over the Orioles in 2019, after they lost an absurd 115 games in 2018. Whatever was left to tear down, he tore down to the studs. They lost 108 games in 2019 and 110 in 2021. Things turned around enough with Elias' rebuild for the Orioles to make the playoffs in both 2023 and 2024, but they were swept out of their series both years and still haven't won a playoff game since 2014. The Orioles are hanging around in contention this season, but it's because the American League is so dreadful. They are five games under .500. That Elias' Orioles were sellers at the trade deadline seems a signal that he plans to go through a rebuild again -- even if not a massive one. Isn't that an admission that the radical rebuild failed? And if that's the case, how is that acceptable?
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Jerry Dipoto, Mariners president of baseball operationsDipoto was hired as the Mariners' general manager in 2015, and he's been the boss on the baseball side ever since. They've only made the playoffs twice in his tenure. Last season was the apex, as the Mariners advanced further than they ever previously had in franchise history, getting to Game 7 of the ALCS (the Mariners are the only team to have never played in the World Series). Following up that effort with a team currently seven games under .500 might be what finally does Dipoto in. Then again, the Mariners are only three games out of first place in the pitiful AL West. Things could still be salvaged. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Scott Harris, Tigers president of baseball operationsThe Tigers waved the white flag at the trade deadline despite being just 2 ½ games out of a playoff spot, trading Tarik Skubal and Casey Mize. They have now fallen apart, losing eight of their last nine games. Harris has been on the job since 2022, and the Tigers have made the playoffs just twice on his watch. They topped out at 87 wins last season, a run that also included blowing a 14-game division lead. 

                            
    
                                                
                    
    David Stearns, Mets president of baseball operationsIn 2024, Stearns' first season with the Mets, they made an unlikely run to the NLCS. Last season, they had the best record in baseball in early June, but fell apart down the stretch and missed the playoffs. Stearns responded by carving up the MLB roster over the winter, and the results have been incredibly disappointing. The Mets sit in last place at 59-72 despite having the second-highest payroll in the majors. To this point, owner Steve Cohen has been nothing but supportive of Stearns, and it seems unlikely a change will be made, but it's difficult to defend Stearns' shaky tenure at this point. You never know if Cohen will change his tune.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Ben Cherington, Pirates general managerCherington has been on the job since 2019. The Pirates' best record with him as boss is 76-86. They might break that this season, but they currently sit 63-69. Cherington actually fixed what was a futile offense this past offseason, but the pitching has fallen apart this time around. Whatever is going on with Paul Skenes should be deemed an organizational failure by ownership, and, really, how many chances should a GM get to win more than 76 games in a season? 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Buster Posey, Giants president of baseball operationsTo be clear, I don't think Giants ownership would ever fire this franchise legend, but it's hard to imagine this partnership lasting forever. After winning 80 games two years ago and finishing at exactly .500 (81-81) last season, the Giants are one of baseball's worst teams this season at 52-78. They are bogged down by some long-term contracts that don't look great (Rafael Devers, Willy Adames, Matt Chapman), and they're headed toward one of their worst finishes in club history. The good news is the farm system looks stronger than it has in a while.

title: Browns name Deshaun Watson starting QB over Shedeur Sanders - CBS Sports
description: Cleveland is giving Watson another opportunity in the final year of his contract after he missed the entire 2025
body:
Cleveland is giving Watson another opportunity in the final year of his contract after he missed the entire 2025 season recovering from Achilles injuries
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                            
        
    Aug 24, 2026
                            
                    at
    10:11 am ET
                        
                •
            
            4 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The Cleveland Browns have named Deshaun Watson the starter for the team's season opener at the Jaguars, beating out Shedeur Sanders for the starting role, per CBS Sports' Matt Zenitz. It will be Watson's first game since Oct. 10, 2024, when he tore his Achilles. He re-tore his Achilles in early January 2025, causing him to miss all of last year.The decision comes just two days after Watson took several shots at Browns fans following his poor performance in preseason Week 2 against the Bills. Watson was just 5 of 12 passing for 35 yards and an interception, playing with (and against) backups in the third and fourth quarters while boos rained down."I think the whole world knows it has nothing to do about the performance," Watson said. "It's a little bit more personal than that. So, I think it's a disrespectful thing."Todd Monken insisted Sunday that the comments wouldn't impact his quarterback choice.
Watson was regarded as a slight leader for much of the quarterback battle, often earning the first reps with the first team, even if the overall reps with the starters ended up somewhat evenly split. Watson started in preseason Week 1 alongside starters, while Sanders started in preseason Week 2 with mostly backups. Even so, Monken, in his first year as a head coach, said the competition played out in "the best way I thought we could go about it."Watson, who turns 31 the day after the Browns' season opener, has been a monumental disappointment in Cleveland, and his acquisition has been regarded as one of the worst in major professional sports history. In 2022, the Browns traded 2022, 2023 and 2024 first-round picks, a third-round pick and two fourth-round picks to the Houston Texans for Watson and a sixth-round pick. The Browns then gave Watson an unprecedented, fully guaranteed five-year, $230 million contract.At the time, Watson faced 22 civil lawsuits related to allegations of sexual misconduct at massage therapy sessions. The number eventually grew to 27. All 27 have been resolved, with at least 24 ending in confidential settlements. The last two were dismissed -- at least one with a settlement -- earlier this year. The Texans also previously reached confidential settlements with 30 women over claims regarding Watson.
Watson did not play at all in his final season in Houston (2021) and was suspended for the first 11 games of 2022 after being traded to Cleveland. In total, he has appeared in just 19 games since the trade, and he was among the NFL's worst quarterbacks when on the field.Deshaun Watson (2022-24)Rank (out of 44)Completion percentage61.2%40thNet yards per attempt5.443rdSack rate11.2%43rdEPA per dropback-0.1943rdThe Browns hope an improved supporting cast helps lift Watson. Cleveland overhauled its offensive line, bringing in four new starters, and drafted wide receiver KC Concepcion in the first round and wide receiver Denzel Boston in the second round. Both have impressed in training camp and are expected to start right away. The Browns also return tight end Harold Fannin Jr. and running back Quinshon Judkins after both had impressive rookie years.This is the final year of Watson's contract.
        
            
                NFL preseason Week 2 winners and losers: Bo Nix shines in return, Deshaun Watson takes shot at Browns fans
                
                    Garrett Podell                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
Why Deshaun Watson won Browns' quarterback battleAs Monken said Saturday, the second preseason game was just another data point in a set of hundreds, ranging far past games and even practices. And as he said Sunday, Watson's comments about the fans wouldn't impact his decision. He appears to have held true to both.Watson had been the front-runner, even if ever so slightly, for quite a bit, according to various reports. His chance to start in the first preseason game, alongside the starters, was an indication of that, even if Monken said both Watson and Sanders would each get a preseason start (something he held true to as well). For as poorly as Watson played Saturday, he held up decently -- nothing special, but nothing disastrous -- the previous week, and Monken described his return to playing football as "awesome."Watson's experience and ability to function in the offense were also keys; after all, he has been in far more NFL offenses, including those with more parallels to Monken's. Furthermore, Watson impressed this offseason with his approach and work ethic, per "NFL on CBS" sideline reporter Aditi Kinkhabwala."In all the years I have been around Deshaun Watson, this is the best that he is mentally," Kinkhabwala told 92.3 The Fan last week. "The space that he is in right now, his focus, the way that he stayed in Cleveland all summer, went to work quietly every day, didn't ask anything of any of the staff in the building at all, was simply focused on living with his wife and working on football and his rehab. Just the conversations I have with him on the side -- different."
It is also worth noting, in light of Watson's most recent comments, that the Browns' first two games -- Week 1 at the Jaguars and Week 2 at the Buccaneers -- are on the road."I feel like I get more love on road games than I do home games," Watson said. "If it is my spot and he does makes me the [starter], maybe it's 17 away games then. I don't know."

title: North Carolina basketball 2026-27 roster breakdown: Starting lineup prediction, bench rotation, outlook - CBS Sports
description: The Tar Heels enter a new era with Michael Malone at the helm of the storied program
body:
The Tar Heels enter a new era with Michael Malone at the helm of the storied program
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Aug 24, 2026
                            
                    at
    11:24 am ET
                        
                •
            
            5 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        North Carolina will enter a new era this season as Michael Malone takes over the program after a lengthy coaching career in the NBA. The former coach of the Sacramento Kings and Denver Nuggets hasn't coached at the college level in over 25 years, with his last stint coming as an assistant coach at Manhattan before making the jump to the NBA in 2001.Following a loss to VCU in the NCAA Tournament, UNC underwent nearly a two-week-long coaching search and landed on Malone despite his lack of ties to the Carolina program, which was an unofficial prerequisite for several coaches who came before him.North Carolina has the No. 8-ranked transfer portal class in the 247Sports rankings, headlined by the additions of Matt Able (NC State), Terrence Brown (Utah) and Neoklis Avdalas (Virginia Tech). The Tar Heels also welcome five-star big man Sayon Keita from Spain, who is a potential name to know for the 2027 NBA Draft.This roster will look drastically different from last season's, which featured star forward Caleb Wilson, the No. 4 overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft. The Tar Heels also lost big man Henri Veesaar to the NBA and defensive ace Seth Trimble, who is set to play for Louisville this season if he is granted an extra year of eligibility.
Let's dive into UNC's roster, starting with who might be in the lineup on opening night against Western Carolina on Nov. 2.North Carolina's projected starting lineupG: Terrence Brown | 6-3 | 180 | Sr.The Utah transfer is coming off a season in which he averaged 19.9 points, 3.8 assists and 2.4 rebounds in his first year playing high-major basketball. Brown began his career at Farleigh Dickinson, where he averaged 20.6 points during the 2024-25 campaign. He will bring scoring, playmaking and much-needed athleticism to UNC's lineup.G: Matt Able | 6-5 | 200 | So.Able is the rare Tobacco Road transfer. Able played last season at NC State and averaged 8.8 points and 3.4 rebounds in just over 21 minutes per game. After appearing in 34 games off the bench for the Wolfpack, Able is set to step into a starting role this season with the Tar Heels. He might be UNC's best NBA prospect and could crack the first round with a breakout season.
G: Neoklis Avdalas | 6-9 | 220 | Fr.The 6-foot-9 guard has the archetype of a point-forward that can be extremely valuable at both the college and NBA levels. As a freshman at Virginia Tech, he averaged 12.1 points, 4.6 assists and 3.1 rebounds in 31 games. There were certainly flashes (see the game against Providence in nonconference play) last season that showed Avdalas can be an impact player.F: Jarin Stevenson | 6-10 | 220 | Sr.Stevenson is one of the lone returners on this roster. The former Alabama forward transferred to UNC ahead of last season and started 25 games for the Tar Heels, averaging 8.1 points and 4.4 rebounds. Stevenson played a key role on Alabama's Final Four team as a reserve in 2024 and should slot into the lineup as the starting power forward.C: Cameron Fens | 7-0 | 255 | Sr.The starting center position could be up for grabs heading into the season, with the top candidates being Fens and Keita. Fens, who was granted an extra year of eligibility via a court ruling in Tennessee, was a late addition to UNC's roster. The former South Dakota big man averaged 14.4 points and 8.7 rebounds per game last season. The burly big man brings experience and heft, which UNC needs, but Keita may be the better long-term option here for the Tar Heels.
Off the benchF: Maximo Adams | 6-7 | 205 | Fr.Adams, the No. 31-ranked playerhttps://247sports.com/player/maximo-adams-46136627/in the 2026 recruiting cycle by 247Sports, stayed true to his pledge despite the coaching change. Adams committed to UNC in November over Texas, Kansas, Michigan State, and Kentucky, among others and signed shortly after. As his 247Sports scouting report notes, he is an "exceptional" mid-range shooter off the dribble.F: Cade Bennerman | 7-0 | 195 | So.Bennerman redshirted during the 2025-26 season at Northwestern and transferred to UNC this offseason. Bennerman was a three-star-rated transfer in the 247Sports rankings and should provide frontcourt depth.C: Sayon Keita | 7-1 | 205 | Fr.Keita has the most NBA upside of anybody on this roster. The projected first-round pick is an athletic 7-footer who can run the floor and protect the rim. Keita should be either UNC's starting center or one of the first players off the bench.
G: Isaiah Denis | 6-4 | 185 | So.Denis appeared in 10 games last season for UNC and could see his role expand with a new-look roster. The former four-star prospect from the 2025 recruiting cycle was the top-ranked player from North Carolina coming out of high school.G: Angelo Brizzi | 6-3 | 200 | Sr.North Carolina will mark Brizzi's fifth school in five years after previous stops at Villanova, Davidson, Longwood and Buffalo. He is coming off the best statistical season of his career after averaging 14.5 points while shooting 37% from the 3-point line this past year at Buffalo.Filling out the rosterF: Jaydon Young | 6-4 | Sr.F: Kevin Thomas | 6-6 | Fr.F: Alexandros Samodurov | 6-11 | Fr.Market watchOdds to win 2027 NCAA Tournament (via FanDuel Sportsbook): +7500 (tied for 32nd-best odds with Villanova)
Vegas is lower on North Carolina heading into this season. However, that projection makes sense because UNC will be ranked in the 20s, or just outside the bubble in the preseason AP Top 25 poll this fall. The Tar Heels have a deeper roster than last season, but they also don't have a blue-chip talent like Wilson. UNC's ceiling will come down to Able and Avdalas taking a Year 2 jump, how good Keita is as a freshman and how quickly Malone adapts to being a college coach.The Tar Heels have a handful of intriguing nonconference games that will be a good measuring stick heading into ACC play. The first test will be on Dec. 1 when UNC hosts Arkansas in the ACC/SEC Challenge. Other games to track include Georgia (Nov. 13), West Virginia (Nov. 27), Butler (Dec. 6), Georgetown (Dec. 12), NC State (Dec. 15), Kentucky (Dec. 19) and Illinois (Jan. 30, 2027).North Carolina will likely be picked to finish fifth in the ACC preseason poll behind Duke, Louisville, Virginia and Miami. The Tar Heels certainly have the talent to be an NCAA Tournament team and make noise in the ACC, but it will come down to those three factors listed in the first paragraph to determine how far UNC can go in March during Malone's first season at the helm.

title: Tennessee names Faizon Brandon starting QB: 5-star freshman to lead Vols in 2026 - CBS Sports
description: The young QB will face big challenges this fall as Tennessee seeks a return to the CFP
body:
The young QB will face big challenges this fall as Tennessee seeks a return to the CFP
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                            
        
    Aug 24, 2026
                            
                    at
    9:12 am ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        After a battle that ran from spring practice through most of fall camp, No. 20 Tennessee has named freshman Faizon Brandon its starting quarterback with under two weeks until the season-opener against Furman, sources confirmed to CBS Sports' Matt Zenitz.A five-star recruit and the No. 2 quarterback in the 2026 signing class, per 247Sports, Brandon didn't wait to make an impression on the coaching staff in Knoxville. Brandon beat out sophomore George MacIntyre -- a blue-chip prospect in his own right -- with strong performances in scrimmages throughout the offseason.In high school, Brandon led Grimsley (N.C.) to consecutive state championships in 2024 and 2025 while posting a 35-1 record as a starter. Throughout his high school career, Brandon threw 90 touchdown passes to just 10 interceptions. Four of those picks came as a freshman, when he played in a backup role.What Brandon lacks in experience, he makes up for in raw talent, and he raises the ceiling of the Tennessee offense. It's up to the other 10 players around him to make sure the flloor is higher with a freshman at the helm.
Brandon will make his first start against Furman on Sept. 5, and while that will be a good opportunity to get his feet wet, the level of difficulty rises sharply in Week 2 with a road game against Georgia Tech. That will be just a taste of what's to come for the young signal caller as Tennessee faces a daunting slate once SEC play begins.Young QB must mature quicklyOutside of games against Furman (Week 1) and Kennesaw State (Week 3), there aren't many opportunities for Tennessee to exhale. That also means Brandon can't afford too many clunkers if the Vols are going to exceed expectations in 2026.The Sept. 12 matchup against the Yellow Jackets isn't exactly a cakewalk, but the real challenge begins when No. 5 Texas rolls into Knoxville two weeks later for the conference opener, and it doesn't get much easier after that. Tennessee faces four teams ranked in the top 15 of the preseason AP poll.
2026 Tennessee schedulevs. Furman (Sept. 5)at Georgia Tech (Sept. 12)vs. Kennesaw State (Sept. 19)vs. No. 5 Texas (Sept. 26)vs. Auburn (Oct. 3)at Arkansas (Oct. 10)vs. No. 13 Alabama (Oct. 17)at South Carolina (Oct. 24)vs. Kentucky (Nov. 7)at No. 8 Texas A&M (Nov. 14)vs. No. 11 LSU (Nov. 21)at Vanderbilt (Nov. 28)Even some of the more winnable SEC games -- like Arkansas and South Carolina -- are on the road. Let's not forget that two of the best Tennessee teams in recent memory lost in those venues. The 2022 Volunteers were upset by the Gamecocks, and the 2024 College Football Playoff team fell to the Razorbacks.For a quarterback making his first college start in less than two weeks, that's a tough draw. The success of Tennessee's season may hinge on how quickly Brandon adapts to life in the SEC.Strong supporting castThe good news for the Volunteers is that the offensive environment for Brandon looks excellent on paper. Tennessee has plenty of experience and returning production on that side of the ball, so that should make life easier on a young quarterback who's just getting his feet wet.
Perhaps most importantly, Tennessee returns 74% of its snaps along the offensive line, and that unit could be one of the best in the entire country. David Sanders Jr. -- an SEC All-Freshman honoree last season -- will protect the blind side at left tackle while center Sam Pendleton anchors the line with 20 career starts.The weapons around Brandon are pretty impressive as well. Wide receivers Mike Matthews and Braylon Staley each topped 800 yards last season, and five-star freshman TK Keys joins that position group in 2026. Accompanying Brandon/Macintyre in the backfield will be running back DeSean Bishop, who totaled 1,211 yards from scrimmage and 16 touchdowns last year.On the whole, the Volunteers return 61% of their offensive snaps from a year ago, which ranks ninth in the country. Starting an inexperienced quarterback against a nine-game SEC schedule may not be ideal, but if ever there was a scenario in which it could work, this is probably it.

title: 2026 NFL All-Breakout Team: Caleb Williams leads rising stars on offense - CBS Sports
description: CBS Sports NFL writers and analysts selected the offensive players poised to take the next step in 2026, with Wil
body:
CBS Sports NFL writers and analysts selected the offensive players poised to take the next step in 2026, with Williams leading a strong contingent of Bears
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Aug 24, 2026
                            
                    at
    10:18 am ET
                        
                •
            
            4 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        NFL breakouts can come from anywhere and anyone. Maybe it's a player coming off a strong close to the previous season. Maybe it's a player finally putting injury woes behind him. Maybe it's the upgraded surroundings that let the player shine. Maybe it's simply a bigger role.Whatever "it" is, breakouts happen every year, whether it's one step up or a few steps up or an elevator to the top floor, like Drake Maye going from inconsistent-but-promising rookie to MVP runner-up. Average players going to good are breakouts, just like good players going to great are breakouts. They come in all shapes and sizes.Thirteen voters, made up of CBS Sports NFL writers and analysts, voted on their All-Breakout Team for 2026, and here are the results for the offensive side of the ball.Voters: JP Acosta, Carter Bahns, John Breech, Doug Clawson, Jordan Dajani, Jared Dubin, Josh Edwards, Zach Pereles, Garrett Podell, Mike Renner, Tyler Sullivan, Ryan Wilson, R.J. White
Quarterback
With four votes, Caleb Williams won a highly competitive vote that featured seven different quarterbacks. The former USC star took a massive jump from a dismal rookie season, especially in avoiding negative play. Williams was also absurdly clutch with an NFL-high six fourth-quarter comebacks. Now, he's the "Madden" cover athlete. Still, there's another level for him to reach, namely in his consistency and accuracy.Others receiving votes: Tyler Shough (3), Jaxson Dart (2), Bo Nix, Bryce Young, Cam Ward, Malik Willis (1 each)Running back
Eight different running backs got at least one vote, but Bhayshul Tuten garnered the most with four. The second-year Jaguars running back only averaged 3.7 yards per carry last year, but he had a 51.8% rushing success rate, 15th out of 67 players with at least 70 carries, and directly in front of James Cook.
Others receiving votes: Ashton Jeanty (2), Omarion Hampton (2), Blake Corum, Jonathon Brooks, Jordan Mason, Quinshon Judkins, TreVeyon Henderson (1 each)Wide receivers
Voters listened when Ben Johnson spoke at the outset of training camp. "I'm buying Luther Burden stock right now," Johnson said in late July. "Just how he's approached his offseason, it's been electric." Burden flashed major talent in limited talent as a rookie, finishing with 652 receiving yards. He'll have a much larger role with DJ Moore now in Buffalo.
The diminutive Josh Downs went from 72 catches and 803 yards in 2024 to just 58 catches and 566 yards last year, but it's easy to see why a resurgence could be in store. The fourth-year pro is in line to see an expanded role after Indianapolis traded Michael Pittman Jr. to the Steelers. Downs playing in two-receiver sets could lead to his first 1,000-yard season. He received five votes.
De'Zhaun Stribling's spot on this team coincides with his excellent preseason. He has 11 catches for 109 yards and looks ready to step into a significant role immediately as the WR2 opposite Mike Evans. San Francisco received a lot of criticism for drafting Stribling No. 33 overall, but all the Ole Miss product has done since is impress. He received four votes.Others receiving votes: Marvin Harrison Jr., Matthew Golden, Parker Washington (3 each), Adonai Mitchell, Jack Bech, Ryan Flournoy (2 each), Darius Cooper, Isaac TeSlaa, Jalen Coker, Jalen McMillan, Rashid Shaheed, Romeo Doubs (1 each)Tight end
NFC North rivals Colston Loveland and Tucker Kraft received three votes apiece to lead the way at tight end. Kraft was on his way to a breakout last year -- 30 catches for 469 yards and six touchdowns through Week 8 -- before tearing his ACL in Week 9. The Loveland selection, on the other hand, is based on a strong finish that included a 137-yard performance in Chicago's playoff win over Green Bay.
Others receiving votes: Gunnar Helm, Chigoziem Okonkwo (2 each), Dalton Kincaid, Mitchell Evans, Isaiah Likely (1 each)Left tackle
Josh Simmons, the No. 32 pick in last year's draft, and Will Campbell, the No. 4 pick in last year's draft, both received four votes. Simmons looked excellent in the eight games he played, but he missed time first due to personal reasons and later due to a season-ending wrist injury.         The Milwaukee Brewers are ridiculous. Again.Remember, the Brewers had the best record in the regular season last year. They lost in the NLCS because the Dodgers went into Terminator Mode for the series, but I think far too many people are assuming that means there would be a repeat this time around, should the two square off again, and I'm not so sure. I think the Brewers can take 'em, if it comes to that. That doesn't much matter right now, though, as we still have more than a month left in the regular season, and this regular season belongs to the Milwaukee Brewers. They didn't start out so hot. They were 13-13 after a loss on April 25. Since then? The Brewers have gone 68-37, a .648 clip (that's a full-season pace of 105 wins). They took three of four games in Dodger Stadium last weekend. They won 22-0 on Tuesday. They won a series over the first-place Braves. On the season, they've gone 4-2 against the Cubs so far, reinforcing their ownership of the NL Central. They swept the Yankees. They've taken two of three from the Rays. 
We could keep going because the Brewers are 43-22 against teams .500 or better. Contained in that 13-13 start were a six-game losing streak and then a four-game losing streak. Since then, the Brewers have only lost more than two straight games three times, and all of those losing streaks were halted at three. They have one of the best defenses in baseball (sitting sixth in defensive efficiency, for example). Despite sitting last in home runs, they are in the top five in batting average and top 10 in OPS, checking in as one of the most prolific run-scoring teams in baseball. They sit third in stolen bases and are one of the best baserunning teams in the league. They are second in the majors in ERA, too. Simply, the Brewers are just awesome at pretty much everything. I do believe they have a good chance to win their first-ever World Series, too. The rotation looks a lot different this season with Jacob Misiorowski at the top, followed by the likes of Logan Henderson, Kyle Harrison and Dustin May.
Doubt the best team in baseball at your peril. They are every bit good enough to win it all.

body:
Superflex leagues clearly favor quarterbacks, but that doesn't mean you have to reach for the position on Draft Day. You can wait for a quarterback or your second quarterback and still build a winning team.  We held a 12-team, PPR, Superflex mock draft Friday with listeners of our Fantasy Football Today Podcast. Alfredo Brown of Reception Perception also took part in this mock draft, along with me and Adam Aizer.  No team started QB-QB in this draft, but three teams drafted two quarterbacks through Round 3. Seven teams had two quarterbacks through Round 5.  I waited until Round 5 to draft my first quarterback, which was Kyler Murray. And Ty Langston waited until Round 6 for his first quarterback, which was Baker Mayfield. Let's look at some different quarterback builds to see what might work best.  Matt Knight had the No. 1 overall pick in this draft, and he started with Jahmyr Gibbs. Matt then went QB-QB at the Rounds 2-3 turn with Jayden Daniels and Brock Purdy, and Matt drafted a third quarterback in Round 7 with Tyler Shough.  Matt ended up with a solid running back corps of Gibbs, Bucky Irving, Jacory Croskey-Merritt, Kyle Monangai, Dylan Sampson and Isiah Pacheco. Matt's receivers are Tetairoa McMillan, Emeka Egbuka and Makai Lemon. And the tight ends are Tucker Kraft and Dallas Goedert.  I don't love this roster because of the receiving corps, and I thought Purdy went too soon. I also would have drafted another receiver instead of Goedert.  Alfredo started his team from the No. 10 spot with Lamar Jackson. Alfredo didn't draft another quarterback until Round 6 with Malik Willis, and those are the only quarterbacks on Alfredo's roster.  His running backs are James Cook, Jonathon Brooks, RJ Harvey, MarShawn Lloyd and Tyjae Spears. Alfredo has Nico Collins, Luther Burden III, Carnell Tate, Jayden Reed, Jalen Coker and Matthew Golden at receiver. And the tight end is Trey McBride.  I like this roster a lot, and this is typically how I would build a Superflex team with one quarterback early and then another with a mid-round pick. I would have preferred if Alfredo drafted a third quarterback, but that's a minor concern.  I drafted three quarterbacks because I needed them after waiting until Round 5 to get Kyler Murray. I then drafted C.J. Stroud in Round 8 and Jacoby Brissett in Round 9.  It was not my intention to draft quarterbacks like this, but I had to alter my plan twice. The first time was in Round 4 when Trevor Lawrence went right before my pick, so I pivoted to Tee Higgins. Then, I expected one of Jaxson Dart, Matthew Stafford or Jared Goff to fall back to me in Round 5, but all three were selected before my pick.  I didn't panic, and instead I tried to build the best roster of running backs, wide receivers and tight ends. My running backs are Kenneth Walker III, Breece Hall, Rachaad White, Jonah Coleman and Keaton Mitchell. My receivers are Puka Nacua, Higgins, Terry McLaurin, Wan'Dale Robinson and Deebo Samuel. And my tight end is Brock Bowers.  I love this team if the quarterbacks are above average. Murray has the chance to be good now that he's in Minnesota, and we'll see if Stroud and Brissett can be successful this year.  Take a look at which quarterback build works for you. Just don't panic if you don't get an elite quarterback in the first four or five rounds.  As a reference point for this mock draft, all touchdowns are worth six points, and we award one point for every 10 yards rushing and receiving and one point for every 25 yards passing. We also award one point for every reception. We feature a starting lineup of QB, 2 RB, 2 WR, TE, 2 FLEX (RB/WR/TE) and a SUPERFLEX (QB/RB/WR/TE) with five reserves for a 14-round draft. body:
I don't know if there's been a more hyped pitching prospect debut in Fantasy than Kade Anderson's since Paul Skenes'. Bubba Chandler a year ago came pretty close, though by the time he actually debuted with the Pirates, it was in a quasi-relief role following months of struggles at Triple-A, so I'm not sure he quite got there. Either way, to say expectations for Anderson have gotten outrageously high over the past month or so would not be an overstatement. And he didn't live up to those expectations in his first MLB start. That's not to say Anderson was bad, because he wasn't – making the leap straight from Double-A and coming up an out short of a quality start against a lineup like the Cubs is pretty impressive, even! But he wasn't transcendent, and that's where the bar was set for many.To start with, Anderson came as advertised in a lot of ways. He showed a deep arsenal and commanded all of it well, throwing all four of his pitches at least 20% of the time and dishing out just two walks despite throwing only 40% of his pitches in the strike zone. That ability to generate chases is a big deal, a sign that he was throwing the ball close enough to the zone to induce swings, but not close enough to risk much damage. For someone who will have to get by more on pitchability and command than pure stuff, already being able to showcase that skill is big.But the stuff is at a relative deficit compared to other high-end pitching prospects. It isn't bad, but it isn't, again, transcendent. Anderson isn't going to come up and blow opposing hitters away, and that is especially true of his four-seamer.
The fastball for Anderson doesn't have bad velocity, but even for a left-handed starter, 93.6 mph isn't exactly special these days. And the jump to the majors seems to have impacted the quality of the pitch – a known issue for any pitcher making the leap from Double-A to the majors at this point. As Lance Brozdowski pointed out in his newsletter Sunday, the ball used at Double-A and lower levels of the minors is different from the one used at MLB and in Triple-A, in a way that often impacts the movement profile and spin rates of fastballs. Anderson's fastball went from having 18.8 inches of induced vertical break (think "rise") in Double-A to just 15.4 inches in his MLB debut. That can be the difference between missing the bat entirely and finding the barrel, and it might mean his mere two whiffs on 27 fastballs weren't just a fluke. That just might not be a great pitch against MLB hitters, especially when Anderson faded down to the 92-ish mph range over his final couple of innings (when he ran into trouble). I don't want to make it seem like I'm too negative about Anderson, because I'm still very excited about what we're going to get from him. He's a lefty with terrific control in an organization (and ballpark!) that so often wrings the most out of its pitchers. He doesn't have an elite fastball, but everything else here looks like it could be at least pretty good, and as we've seen in recent years, lefties can often perform better than you might expect by dint of being, for lack of a better word, funky. 
But Anderson has been talked about as a potential immediate impact arm for Fantasy for months. I've seen commenters on FBT, for example, talk about him as a top-10 pitcher in baseball before he even made his MLB debut. People were complaining that Scott White and Frank Stampfl only talked about him as a top-40 starting pitcher when he got the call this week. When that's how high the expectations are, you do have to nitpick. And Anderson may not quite have the stuff to match up with some of the other most exciting young pitchers in baseball.That doesn't mean he can't be good. Heck, it doesn't mean he can't live up to those lofty expectations, even – Parker Messick is a top-10 pitcher in Fantasy this season with a pretty similar profile, in fact. It's just one start, after all, and we shouldn't draw any strong conclusions on the basis of just one start, especially for someone who was pretty historically dominant at Double-A.But if you assumed Anderson was simply going to step onto an MLB mound and immediately pitch like an ace, that might not be in the cards for him based on what we saw in his MLB debut.

 	Three Up Blake Snell is rolling You never quite know what you're going to get from Snell. He'll routinely have stretches where he looks like the best pitcher in baseball, but he'll just as often look like an absolute mess. Toss in the year IL stint (or two) and a lot of Fantasy players have rightly decided he isn't worth the trouble. Buy boy, when he's right, it sure is exciting, isn't it? And Snell looks really right since his return from elbow surgery, as he tossed his third excellent start in a row Sunday against the Pirates, limiting them to just two hits and three walks across six shutout innings. Across his three starts, Snell has 21 strikeouts to just seven hits and seven walks in 18 innings, while allowing a 1.00 ERA in that span. And the thing about Snell is that while the overall experience of having him on your roster can be exhausting, once he gets rolling, it tends to take an injury to stop him. He looks poised to help carry some folks to a Fantasy championship down the stretch, and while I don't think I'll ever be able to justify drafting him as a top-30 SP – especially not on a Dodgers team whose only goal is being healthy in October – he's in the midst of reminding us of exactly why someone will be willing to justify that price every spring. Fernando Tatis is himself againIt seems pretty clear at this point that Tatis just screwed up his swing early in the season. Every player tinkers to try to find an edge, and the early part of this season isn't the only time we've ever seen Tatis tinker with his swing, but the results this time were simply catastrophic. He was still generating huge exit velocities, but he just couldn't drive the ball in the air to the right parts of the field, which is how he went over two months at the start of the season without homering. Maybe it isn't all about his swing setup, but when you compare Tatis' setup in 2025, then the first two months of 2026, and then ever since, it's not hard to draw a pretty strong conclusion here. Whatever caused it, Tatis has looked like his usual self since the beginning of June, and he was absurdly locked in this weekend, going 9 for 14 with two homers in a three-game series with the Twins, and he's now hitting .316/.391/.737 in August with nine homers. It's not impossible that Tatis could finish the season with 25 homers and 40 steals, pretty much exactly what you drafted him to be. That seems inconceivable after his awful first two months, but it's a good reminder to not give up on elite talents, no matter how poorly they are playing. Spencer Jones is starting to show flashesCredit where it's due to Jones, who is managing to make an impact in spite of his limitations. He only went 3 for 9 this weekend, but he had five hits in his previous three games and has two homers and two steals in his past six games, while striking out a pretty reasonable eight times in 27 at-bats. Overall, there is still too much swing-and-miss in Jones' game, though even if you zoom out, he's at least approaching respectability there, with a 32.6% strikeout rate so far in August. With his power and athleticism, a 33% strikeout rate might be workable for Jones. He isn't a star and likely won't develop into one, and there is still some very real bottom-out potential, but he's looking a lot more viable than I expected. 
 	Three Down Nick Lodolo is finishedThere's no question that Lodolo is a talented pitcher, but I think we've gotta admit at this point that it just isn't going to happen for him this season. His recurring blister issues have completely derailed his season, to the point where he has had to completely alter how he throws his breaking ball just to stay on the mound. Unfortunately, nothing he has tried has worked out, as he got tagged for six earned runs in 3.1 innings in his start this weekend to push his ERA to 7.30 since his latest return from the IL. He just hasn't been right at all this season and I see no reason to think he's going to suddenly turn it around. He's 66% rostered right now, and that makes him one of the most over-rostered players in Fantasy. He's gotta find another way to overcome these blister issues this offseason. Bryce Miller is droppable Miller is probably Lodolo's main competition for "most over-rostered player in Fantasy right now," and the only thing keeping Miller from running away with it is the fact that he was actually very good at one point this season. But that was a pretty long time ago at this point, as Miller has a 7.19 ERA and 1.62 WHIP over his past eight starts, with 30 strikeouts and 20 walks in 41.1 innings in that span. That earlier stretch of dominance did happen, so we can't totally foreclose on the possibility that he could flip a switch and get back to it. But we're at the point in the season where you can't really afford to wait it out with a player struggling this badly, so I'm inclined to view Miller as a drop in nearly all leagues. Especially leagues where Andrew Painter or Jacob Lopez are available. Joshua Baez is looking overmatchedBaez's MLB debut couldn't have gone much better, as he slugged three homers in his first game against the Cubs last week. Things couldn't have gone much worse since, however. He went 0 for 4 with two strikeouts Sunday and is now hitting just .063 with one homer and 14 strikeouts in nine games since that debut. Even with the three-homer game, he has just an 83 wRC+, and while that doesn't necessarily mean he's going to struggle forever – his underlying numbers are still quite good thanks to his plus power – it does suggest there is going to be a steeper learning curve here than you might have hoped. I still think Baez is worth rostering in basically all formats for what it might look like when everything clicks, but he's definitely not someone you need to be starting just yet. 
 	Extra Innings The National League MVP race isn't over yetIf the season ended today, Pete Crow-Armstrong would have to be the NL MVP. He's putting together an all-time great defensive season while leaping from being a pretty good hitter to one of the best in baseball, and he's showing no signs of slowing down – he homered Friday and Sunday this weekend and has six in his past seven and nine in the month of August already. This isn't a case of voter fatigue or whatever bad-faith nonsense people want to throw out about why Shohei Ohtani actually deserves it over PCA; PCA is just having that good of a season. But here's the thing: The season doesn't end today! It doesn't end for another 35 days, in fact! There is still about 20% of the schedule left to be played, which is a lot of time! Nobody has to decide who the MVP is right now, especially when Ohtani is about to get back on the mound. There probably isn't much Ohtani can do as a DH alone to overcome Crow-Armstrong's all-around dominance, especially when he is now a net-neutral contributor on the bases. But if he throws another 20 innings of sub-2.00-ERA ball? He could absolutely close the gap. He's the underdog right now, to be sure, and that's a weird spot to see Shohei Ohtani in. But just ask those anonymous scouts who said he was a "high-school hitter" how betting against him tends to work out.
